unresolved_critical_ir.description: Ligase seals the nick between gap_fill and fragment_1, but these two DNA objects have overlapping/extending geometry (gap_fill end coincident with fragment_1 start at x=-1.2, yet gap_fill was extended from -0.6 to -1.2 while fragment_1 extends from -1.2 to -3.5). The connection is between the correct biology endpoints, but the ligase is attached to gap_fill at its growing 3' end rather than at the actual nick between gap_fill and fragment_1, and no target anchor pairing (gap_fill.end ↔ fragment_1.start) is visibly established by a common junction. The covalent seal 'connect' transitions use anchor pairs whose coincidence is asserted by the deterministic checker but the drawn geometry shows the two strands merged into a single pass-through line; the sealing junction is not depicted as a true nick being closed.
unresolved_critical_ir.repair_scope: Re-anchor the ligase active site to the gap_fill.end ↔ fragment_1.start nick and ensure the sealed_nick relation is created exactly at that junction, with both DNA segments meeting end-to-end (not overlapping) so the seal is a visible nick closure.
acceptance_criteria: ligase attaches to the shared endpoint of gap_fill.end and fragment_1.start, not gap_fill.center or growing end.
gap_fill.end and fragment_1.start are coincident within tolerance 0.03 before sealing and remain a single contiguous strand after sealing; no overhang or overlap is drawn.
The sealed_nick relation is between exactly gap_fill → fragment_1 at those anchors.

unresolved_critical_ir.description: In event_4, primase is shown synthesizing the lagging-strand primer rna_primer_lagging_1 centered at [-0.9, -0.386] and rna_primer_lagging_2 at [1.4, -0.064], but these visual centers sit off the template_lagging strand (y=-0.95 for the paired region). RNA primers are objects on the template, so their schematic position should be adjacent to their template footprints at y≈-0.95, not floating above/below the strand by ~0.56–0.89 units. The primer_extension_continuity relations bind primer 'start'/'end' to fragment 'start', but the primer polylines are drawn at y=-0.95 while object centers used for the primase binding are at y=-0.386/-0.064, which is ambiguous about which primer footprint is being extended.
unresolved_critical_ir.repair_scope: Keep the primase enzyme center offset above the strand for readability, but place the RNA primer polylines on the template_lagging strand at the footprint of the new fragment (y≈-0.95) so primer_extension_continuity endpoints are geometrically genuine adjacent endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: rna_primer_lagging_1 points lie on/near template_lagging (y within 0.05 of the strand) at the fragment_1 footprint x-range, and rna_primer_lagging_2 similarly at the fragment_2 footprint.
primer_extension_continuity relation between primer end and fragment start uses genuine adjacent endpoints (measured distance ≤0.03).
